one_fix: In the problem block, replace the first two sentences ('Since February 2025 ... The consultation questionnaire alone is not enough.') with one cost-first sentence that quotes the rule accurately: 'Since February 2025, GPhC guidance has required prescribers of weight-management medicines to verify weight, height and/or BMI independently of the patient's questionnaire answers, so every order supplied on declared weight alone is a prescribing decision the pharmacy may have to defend at inspection or in answer to a concern.' Then delete the closing sentence that repeats that point ('Each order approved on declared weight alone ...'). This puts the cost before the numbers, restores the regulator's word 'independently' and cuts about 25 words of the overrun.

points_lost.Proof of belonging to the vertical: Good GPhC, PMR, superintendent and re-order detail. But no number from this vertical in the hero (the proof strip is generic product facts), US-only AWS hosting goes unaddressed for a UK buyer beyond the SCCs line, and the 'including an online pharmacy' caption is the only vertical proof.
points_lost.Claims discipline: The GPhC paraphrase drops 'independently', the guidance's key qualifier, in a way that flatters a check built on patient-entered height. 'Results kept private' presents hiding weight from the patient as a privacy benefit. 'Speaks to that last concern more directly' implies resistance to manipulation without evidence.
points_lost.Sales argument: The H1 outcome ('a live weight check') describes the product, not what the pharmacy pays for (defensible, GPhC-ready prescribing without losing orders). The problem block opens with regulation instead of cost and ends on a soft 'may have to defend'. How-it-works step 1 gives the actor no benefit. Visible copy is 1,632 words, over the 1,600 budget.
points_lost.Uniqueness against the parent: The GPhC framing and statistics are the subject of the linked hub compliance guide, and the page overlaps the /for-bmi-verification/ feature page it calls 'the feature behind the check'. The cannibalisation risk is real, and the 60% rule cannot be confirmed.
points_lost.Conversion: Measured button gaps of about 1,870 px and 2,420 px (the accuracy block) break 'a CTA on every second screen' at 800 px. The analytics events are unverified. The demo block does not say what happens after the form is submitted.
points_lost.Copy in the buyer's language: The biggest operational pain, the staff time and checkout drop-off of manual video, GP-record or scale-photo checks, appears only as a pilot metric and never in the buyer's words. US spelling ('anonymized') on a UK-targeted page, and 'weight-loss medication' is mixed with the GPhC's 'weight management medicines'.
points_lost.Human copy: The appended 'with no ...' benefit clause recurs six times across sections. Bold-label-plus-one-sentence cards make several blocks read as a filled template. The lede line 'runs these weight checks for online pharmacies' reads as keyword-stuffed. The opinion ('the evidence belongs with the order') and the boundaries do save it.
points_lost.Search and AI visibility: The focus keyphrase 'weight checks for online pharmacies' (and 'Order-Flow Weight Checks' in the title) is an unnatural, likely low-volume query, and the H1 does not carry it exactly. The FAQ H3s are brand-specific ('How does FitXpress fit ...'), not GEO search phrasing. The schema 'mentions' point to @ids on other pages that may not exist.
points_lost.Place in the site and technical layer: No link up (excused while the parent page redirects), and the siblings are a single 'Related pages' line, not cards. Performance was not measured and no full tab-through was done. The URL is already planned to 301 to /fitxpress/for-online-pharmacies/ after launch, while hub articles target that path's #demo.
